title: HARNESS: Lightweight Distilled Arabic Speech Foundation Models
summary: Large self-supervised speech (SSL) models achieve strong downstream performance, but their size limits deployment in resource-constrained settings. We present HArnESS, an Arabic-centric self-supervised speech model family trained from scratch with iterative self-distillation, together with lightweight student variants that offer strong accuracy-efficiency trade-offs on Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR), Dialect Identification (DID), and Speech Emotion Recognition (SER). Our approach begins with a large bilingual Arabic-English teacher and progressively distills its knowledge into compressed student models while preserving Arabic-relevant acoustic and paralinguistic representations. We further study PCA-based compression of the teacher supervision signal to better match the capacity of shallow and thin students. Compared with HuBERT and XLS-R, HArnESS consistently improves performance on Arabic downstream tasks, while the compressed models remain competitive under substantial structural reduction. These results position HArnESS as a practical and accessible Arabic-centric SSL foundation for real-world speech applications.

AI.tldr: HArnESS is an Arabic-centric self-supervised speech model family trained from scratch with iterative self-distillation, offering strong accuracy-efficiency trade-offs for Arabic speech tasks.
AI.motivation: Large self-supervised speech models achieve strong performance but their size limits deployment in resource-constrained settings, especially for Arabic-centric applications where specialized models are needed.
AI.method: Train a large bilingual Arabic-English teacher model from scratch, then use iterative self-distillation to create compressed student variants. Apply PCA-based compression of teacher supervision signals to better match student capacity.
AI.result: HArnESS consistently improves performance on Arabic downstream tasks (ASR, DID, SER) compared to HuBERT and XLS-R. Compressed models remain competitive under substantial structural reduction.
AI.conclusion: HArnESS serves as a practical and accessible Arabic-centric SSL foundation for real-world speech applications, offering strong accuracy-efficiency trade-offs.

title: Who is Speaking or Who is Depressed? A Controlled Study of Speaker Leakage in Speech-Based Depression Detection
summary: This study investigates whether speech-based depression detection models learn depression-related acoustic biomarkers or instead rely on speaker identity cues. Using the DAIC-WOZ dataset, we propose a data-splitting strategy that controls speaker overlap between training and test sets while keeping the training size constant, and evaluate three models of varying complexity. Results show that speaker overlap significantly boosts performance, whereas accuracy drops sharply on unseen speakers. Even with a Domain-Adversarial Neural Network, a substantial performance gap remains. These findings indicate that depression-related features extracted by current speech models are highly entangled with speaker identity. Conventional evaluation protocols may therefore overestimate generalization and clinical utility, highlighting the need for strictly speaker-independent evaluation.

AI.tldr: Current speech-based depression detection models rely heavily on speaker identity cues rather than learning genuine depression-related acoustic biomarkers, as shown by significant performance drops on unseen speakers despite speaker overlap boosting results.
AI.motivation: To determine whether speech-based depression detection models actually learn depression-related acoustic biomarkers or simply rely on speaker identity cues, which would compromise their clinical utility and generalization to new patients.
AI.method: Used DAIC-WOZ dataset with a novel data-splitting strategy controlling speaker overlap between training and test sets while keeping training size constant. Evaluated three models of varying complexity and implemented a Domain-Adversarial Neural Network to disentangle speaker identity from depression features.
AI.result: Speaker overlap significantly boosts model performance, while accuracy drops sharply on unseen speakers. Even with Domain-Adversarial Neural Networks, a substantial performance gap remains between seen and unseen speakers.
AI.conclusion: Depression-related features extracted by current speech models are highly entangled with speaker identity. Conventional evaluation protocols overestimate generalization and clinical utility, necessitating strictly speaker-independent evaluation for reliable depression detection systems.

title: UniPASE: A Generative Model for Universal Speech Enhancement with High Fidelity and Low Hallucinations
summary: Universal speech enhancement (USE) aims to restore speech signals from diverse distortions across multiple sampling rates. We propose UniPASE, an extension of the low-hallucination PASE framework tailored for USE. At its core is DeWavLM-Omni, a unified representation-level enhancement module fine-tuned from WavLM via knowledge distillation on a large-scale supervised multi-distortion dataset. This module directly converts degraded waveforms into clean and linguistically faithful phonetic representations, ensuring robust enhancement with minimal linguistic hallucination. Based on these enhanced phonetic representations, an Adapter generates enhanced acoustic representations containing rich acoustic details, which a neural Vocoder uses to reconstruct corresponding high-fidelity 16-kHz waveforms. A PostNet then converts the waveforms to 48~kHz before resampling them to their original rates, enabling seamless handling of inputs and outputs at multiple sampling rates. Experimental results on several evaluation datasets, covering sub-tasks and full tasks, demonstrate that UniPASE achieves superior or competitive performance compared with existing state-of-the-art models. The proposed model also serves as the backbone of our submission to the URGENT 2026 Challenge, which achieved 1st place in the objective evaluation. The source code and audio demos are available at https://github.com/xiaobin-rong/unipase/.

AI.tldr: UniPASE is a universal speech enhancement framework that extends PASE to handle diverse distortions across multiple sampling rates, achieving state-of-the-art performance and winning the URGENT 2026 Challenge.
AI.motivation: Universal speech enhancement needs to handle diverse distortions across multiple sampling rates while maintaining linguistic fidelity and minimizing hallucination.
AI.method: Extends PASE framework with DeWavLM-Omni (unified representation-level enhancement module fine-tuned from WavLM via knowledge distillation), Adapter for acoustic details, neural Vocoder for waveform reconstruction, and PostNet for multi-rate handling.
AI.result: Achieves superior/competitive performance on evaluation datasets covering sub-tasks and full tasks; won 1st place in objective evaluation of URGENT 2026 Challenge.
AI.conclusion: UniPASE provides an effective universal speech enhancement solution with robust performance across distortions and sampling rates, serving as a strong backbone for practical applications.

title: From Black Box to Glass Box: Cross-Model ASR Disagreement to Prioto Review in Ambient AI Scribe Documentation
summary: Ambient AI "scribe" systems promise to reduce clinical documentation burden, but automatic speech recognition (ASR) errors can remain unnoticed without careful review, and high-quality human reference transcripts are often unavailable for calibrating uncertainty. We investigate whether cross-model disagreement among heterogeneous ASR systems can act as a reference-free uncertainty signal to prioritize human verification in medical transcription workflows. Using 50 publicly available medical education audio clips (8 h 14 min), we transcribed each clip with eight ASR systems spanning commercial APIs and open-source engines. We aligned multi-model outputs, built consensus pseudo-references, and quantified token-level agreement using a majority-strength metric; we further characterized disagreements by type (content vs. punctuation/formatting) and assessed per-model agreement via leave-one-model-out (jackknife) consensus scoring. Inter-model reliability was low (ICC[2,1] = 0.131), indicating heterogeneous failure modes across systems. Across 76,398 evaluated token positions, 72.1% showed near-unanimous agreement (7-8 models), while 2.5% fell into high-risk bands (0-3 models), with high-risk mass varying from 0.7% to 11.4% across accent groups. Low-agreement regions were enriched for content disagreements, with the content fraction increasing from 53.9% to 73.9% across quintiles of high-risk mass. These results suggest that cross-model disagreement provides a sparse, localizable signal that can surface potentially unreliable transcript spans without human-verified references, enabling targeted review; clinical accuracy of flagged regions remains to be established.

AI.tldr: Cross-model disagreement among heterogeneous ASR systems provides reference-free uncertainty signal for prioritizing human verification in medical transcription workflows.
AI.motivation: Ambient AI scribe systems reduce documentation burden but ASR errors can go unnoticed without careful review, and high-quality human reference transcripts are often unavailable for calibrating uncertainty.
AI.method: Used 50 medical education audio clips (8h14min), transcribed with eight heterogeneous ASR systems (commercial APIs and open-source engines). Aligned multi-model outputs, built consensus pseudo-references, quantified token-level agreement using majority-strength metric, characterized disagreements by type (content vs. punctuation/formatting), assessed per-model agreement via leave-one-model-out consensus scoring.
AI.result: Inter-model reliability was low (ICC[2,1] = 0.131), indicating heterogeneous failure modes. Across 76,398 token positions: 72.1% showed near-unanimous agreement (7-8 models), 2.5% fell into high-risk bands (0-3 models). High-risk mass varied from 0.7% to 11.4% across accent groups. Low-agreement regions enriched for content disagreements (content fraction increased from 53.9% to 73.9% across quintiles of high-risk mass).
AI.conclusion: Cross-model disagreement provides sparse, localizable signal that can surface potentially unreliable transcript spans without human-verified references, enabling targeted review; clinical accuracy of flagged regions remains to be established.

title: End-to-End Learning-based Operation of Integrated Energy Systems for Buildings and Data Centers
summary: Buildings and data centers (DCs) are energy-intensive sectors, playing a critical role to achieve the low-carbon and sustainable energy transition targets. To this end, integrated energy system (IES) that incorporates diverse renewables, energy generation, conversion, and storage technologies to enable coordinated multi-energy supply have been widely investigated for both buildings and DCs. However, few works consider the two sectors jointly within IES to exploit their substantial synergistic benefits. Meanwhile, the operational optimization of IES remains challenging due to the difficulty to predict the multi-energy demand and supply accurately. To address these gaps, this paper investigates IES for coordinated multi-energy supply of buildings and DC, where the waste heat from DCs is recovered and reused to enhance energy efficiency. Moreover, an end-to-end learning-based method is proposed for the operational optimization of IES under uncertainty. Unlike conventional predict-then-optimize approaches, the proposed method integrates the training of prediction models for uncertain variables with the constrained optimization of IES into a unified learning framework, guiding the training of prediction models to improve operational performance, rather than prediction accuracy, thereby mitigating the impacts of predictions errors. Case studies based on real-world datasets show that the proposed methods improves the operational performance of IES by about 7-9% compared to existing predict-then-optimize methods. In addition, coordinating buildings and DCs within IES shows substantial economic benefits. In particular, the waste heat recovery from DCs leads to approximately 10% of total energy cost reduction of the IES.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes an end-to-end learning-based method for optimizing integrated energy systems (IES) that coordinate buildings and data centers, using waste heat recovery from DCs to enhance energy efficiency and reduce costs.
AI.motivation: Buildings and data centers are energy-intensive sectors crucial for achieving low-carbon energy transition targets. While integrated energy systems have been studied for both sectors separately, few works consider them jointly to exploit synergistic benefits. Additionally, operational optimization of IES is challenging due to difficulties in accurately predicting multi-energy demand and supply.
AI.method: The paper investigates IES for coordinated multi-energy supply of buildings and data centers, incorporating waste heat recovery from DCs. It proposes an end-to-end learning-based method that integrates prediction model training for uncertain variables with constrained optimization of IES into a unified framework, focusing on improving operational performance rather than just prediction accuracy.
AI.result: Case studies based on real-world datasets show the proposed method improves IES operational performance by 7-9% compared to existing predict-then-optimize methods. Coordinating buildings and DCs within IES shows substantial economic benefits, with waste heat recovery from DCs leading to approximately 10% reduction in total energy costs.
AI.conclusion: The integrated approach of coordinating buildings and data centers within IES, combined with the end-to-end learning-based optimization method, significantly enhances energy efficiency and economic performance while addressing prediction uncertainty challenges in IES operations.

title: Disentangled Dual-Branch Graph Learning for Conversational Emotion Recognition
summary: Multimodal emotion recognition in conversations aims to infer utterance-level emotions by jointly modeling textual, acoustic, and visual cues within context. Despite recent progress, key challenges remain, including redundant cross-modal information, imperfect semantic alignment, and insufficient modeling of high-order speaker interactions. To address these issues, we propose a framework that combines dual-space feature disentanglement with dual-branch graph learning. A shared encoder and modality-specific encoders are used to separate modality-invariant and modality-specific representations. The invariant features are modeled by a Fourier graph neural network to capture global consistency and complementary patterns, with a frequency-domain contrastive objective to enhance discriminability. In parallel, a speaker-aware hypergraph is constructed over modality-specific features to model high-order interactions, along with a speaker-consistency constraint to maintain coherent semantics. Finally, the two branches are fused for utterance-level emotion prediction. Experiments on IEMOCAP and MELD demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior performance over strong baselines, validating its effectiveness.

AI.tldr: A multimodal emotion recognition framework combining dual-space feature disentanglement with dual-branch graph learning to address cross-modal redundancy, semantic misalignment, and insufficient speaker interaction modeling.
AI.motivation: To address key challenges in multimodal emotion recognition: redundant cross-modal information, imperfect semantic alignment between modalities, and insufficient modeling of high-order speaker interactions in conversations.
AI.method: Proposes a framework with: 1) Shared and modality-specific encoders for disentangling modality-invariant and modality-specific representations; 2) Fourier graph neural network on invariant features with frequency-domain contrastive objective; 3) Speaker-aware hypergraph on modality-specific features with speaker-consistency constraint; 4) Fusion of both branches for final prediction.
AI.result: Superior performance over strong baselines on IEMOCAP and MELD datasets, validating the effectiveness of the proposed approach.
AI.conclusion: The combination of dual-space feature disentanglement with dual-branch graph learning effectively addresses key challenges in multimodal emotion recognition, achieving state-of-the-art performance on benchmark datasets.

title: Energetic Resilience under Temporal Logic Specifications
summary: In environments with uncertainties or undesirable influences, control systems can require additional energy to achieve their task while remaining resilient to these influences. In this paper, we present an energetic resilience metric that quantifies the maximal additional energy used by a system under undesired effects, while satisfying complex specifications encoded through temporal logic. We prove that this metric satisfies properties that enable its computation even for compositions of these specifications, thus allowing considerations of sequential reachability and safety tasks. For specifications related to finite-horizon reachability and safety, we describe how synthesizing a control input and computing this metric reduces to solving efficient quadratic programs. Two case studies on a fighter-jet model and a planar mobile robot illustrate how the synthesized control inputs satisfy given specifications despite undesired and potentially adversarial effects. Further, we demonstrate how the energetic resilience metric varies with the initial state as well as the magnitude of undesired effects.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces an energetic resilience metric that quantifies the maximal additional energy a control system needs to satisfy temporal logic specifications despite uncertainties or adversarial influences, with efficient computation methods and case study demonstrations.
AI.motivation: Control systems operating in uncertain environments with undesirable influences require additional energy to achieve tasks while maintaining resilience. There's a need to quantify this additional energy expenditure in a way that accounts for complex specifications encoded through temporal logic.
AI.method: The authors propose an energetic resilience metric that measures maximal additional energy used under undesired effects while satisfying temporal logic specifications. They prove properties enabling computation for specification compositions. For finite-horizon reachability and safety specifications, they reduce control synthesis and metric computation to solving efficient quadratic programs.
AI.result: Two case studies on a fighter-jet model and planar mobile robot demonstrate that synthesized control inputs satisfy given specifications despite undesired/adversarial effects. The energetic resilience metric varies with initial state and magnitude of undesired effects, providing quantitative resilience assessment.
AI.conclusion: The proposed energetic resilience metric effectively quantifies additional energy requirements for control systems under uncertainties while satisfying complex temporal logic specifications, with efficient computational methods and practical applicability demonstrated through case studies.

title: VoxSafeBench: Not Just What Is Said, but Who, How, and Where
summary: As speech language models (SLMs) transition from personal devices into shared, multi-user environments, their responses must account for far more than the words alone. Who is speaking, how they sound, and where the conversation takes place can each turn an otherwise benign request into one that is unsafe, unfair, or privacy-violating. Existing benchmarks, however, largely focus on basic audio comprehension, study individual risks in isolation, or conflate content that is inherently harmful with content that only becomes problematic due to its acoustic context. We introduce VoxSafeBench, among the first benchmarks to jointly evaluate social alignment in SLMs across three dimensions: safety, fairness, and privacy. VoxSafeBench adopts a Two-Tier design: Tier1 evaluates content-centric risks using matched text and audio inputs, while Tier2 targets audio-conditioned risks in which the transcript is benign but the appropriate response hinges on the speaker, paralinguistic cues, or the surrounding environment. To validate Tier2, we include intermediate perception probes and confirm that frontier SLMs can successfully detect these acoustic cues yet still fail to act on them appropriately. Across 22 tasks with bilingual coverage, we find that safeguards appearing robust on text often degrade in speech: safety awareness drops for speaker- and scene-conditioned risks, fairness erodes when demographic differences are conveyed vocally, and privacy protections falter when contextual cues arrive acoustically. Together, these results expose a pervasive speech grounding gap: current SLMs frequently recognize the relevant social norm in text but fail to apply it when the decisive cue must be grounded in speech. Code and data are publicly available at: https://amphionteam.github.io/VoxSafeBench_demopage/

AI.tldr: VoxSafeBench is a benchmark for evaluating social alignment in speech language models across safety, fairness, and privacy dimensions, revealing that text-based safeguards often degrade when acoustic context is involved.
AI.motivation: As speech language models move into multi-user environments, their responses must account for acoustic context (speaker identity, vocal characteristics, environment) that can turn benign requests into unsafe, unfair, or privacy-violating situations. Existing benchmarks focus on basic audio comprehension, study individual risks in isolation, or conflate content that is inherently harmful with content that only becomes problematic due to acoustic context.
AI.method: VoxSafeBench uses a Two-Tier design: Tier1 evaluates content-centric risks using matched text and audio inputs, while Tier2 targets audio-conditioned risks where transcripts are benign but appropriate responses depend on speaker identity, paralinguistic cues, or environmental context. The benchmark includes 22 tasks with bilingual coverage and incorporates intermediate perception probes to validate Tier2 by confirming that SLMs can detect acoustic cues but fail to act on them appropriately.
AI.result: The study finds that safeguards appearing robust on text often degrade in speech: safety awareness drops for speaker- and scene-conditioned risks, fairness erodes when demographic differences are conveyed vocally, and privacy protections falter when contextual cues arrive acoustically. Frontier SLMs can successfully detect acoustic cues but still fail to act on them appropriately, exposing a pervasive speech grounding gap.
AI.conclusion: Current speech language models frequently recognize relevant social norms in text but fail to apply them when decisive cues must be grounded in speech, highlighting a critical gap in speech grounding that needs to be addressed for safe deployment in multi-user environments.

title: Consensus and Synchronization of Multi-agent Systems over Finite Fields -- Graph Topologies
comment: This work was co-funded by the European Union under the project ROBOPROX (reg. no. CZ.02.01.01/00/22_008/0004590)
summary: This paper brings cooperative protocols for multi-agent systems with agents having a finite state-space. Both scalar single-integrator consensus and general LTI systems synchronization are considered. Systems having a finite state-space describe agents with minimal memory capacity processing only a finite alphabet. Such systems are remarkably resilient to communication noise. The crucial problem, however, is to construct the admissible communication topology, which is NP-hard. We address this by efficiently exploring the subsets of admissible matrices and propose two new algorithms to generate the topologies. Simulations validate the proposed approach.

AI.tldr: Efficient algorithms for generating admissible communication topologies in finite state-space multi-agent systems, addressing NP-hard topology construction for consensus and synchronization protocols.
AI.motivation: Finite state-space multi-agent systems offer resilience to communication noise but face the NP-hard problem of constructing admissible communication topologies, requiring efficient solutions.
AI.method: Proposes two new algorithms that efficiently explore subsets of admissible matrices to generate communication topologies for both scalar single-integrator consensus and general LTI system synchronization.
AI.result: Simulations validate the proposed approach, demonstrating successful topology generation for finite state-space multi-agent systems.
AI.conclusion: The paper provides practical algorithms to overcome the NP-hard topology construction problem in finite state-space multi-agent systems, enabling their implementation with noise resilience benefits.

title: The Acoustic Camouflage Phenomenon: Re-evaluating Speech Features for Financial Risk Prediction
summary: In computational paralinguistics, detecting cognitive load and deception from speech signals is a heavily researched domain. Recent efforts have attempted to apply these acoustic frameworks to corporate earnings calls to predict catastrophic stock market volatility. In this study, we empirically investigate the limits of acoustic feature extraction (pitch, jitter, and hesitation) when applied to highly trained speakers in in-the-wild teleconference environments. Utilizing a two-stream late-fusion architecture, we contrast an acoustic-based stream with a baseline Natural Language Processing (NLP) stream. The isolated NLP model achieved a recall of 66.25% for tail-risk downside events. Surprisingly, integrating acoustic features via late fusion significantly degraded performance, reducing recall to 47.08%. We identify this degradation as Acoustic Camouflage, where media-trained vocal regulation introduces contradictory noise that disrupts multimodal meta-learners. We present these findings as a boundary condition for speech processing applications in high-stakes financial forecasting.

AI.tldr: Acoustic features (pitch, jitter, hesitation) from corporate earnings calls degrade financial risk prediction performance due to "Acoustic Camouflage" - media-trained vocal regulation introduces contradictory noise that disrupts multimodal models.
AI.motivation: To investigate the limits of acoustic feature extraction when applied to highly trained speakers in real-world teleconference environments, specifically for predicting catastrophic stock market volatility from corporate earnings calls.
AI.method: Two-stream late-fusion architecture contrasting acoustic-based stream (pitch, jitter, hesitation features) with baseline NLP stream, applied to corporate earnings calls to predict tail-risk downside events.
AI.result: Isolated NLP model achieved 66.25% recall for tail-risk events, but integrating acoustic features via late fusion significantly degraded performance to 47.08% recall, revealing "Acoustic Camouflage" phenomenon.
AI.conclusion: Media-trained vocal regulation introduces contradictory noise that disrupts multimodal meta-learners, establishing a boundary condition for speech processing applications in high-stakes financial forecasting.

title: Probabilistic Connectivity Analysis of Recursive Satellite Release for Formation Initialization
comment: Accepted for presentation at the 2026 IEEE Aerospace Conference
summary: In the initial deployment of large-scale distributed space systems using small satellites, achieving a reliable transition to passively stable orbits while maintaining inter-satellite distances within effective control and communication ranges is crucial, particularly given the presence of deployment errors and uncontrolled coasting phases. This study presents a framework for designing formation initialization that provides probabilistic safety guarantees. The scope covers the initial deployment phase, from sequential release by a single carrier to commissioning, control activation, and transition to passive stabilization. Strict separation limits during initialization necessitate low release velocities to minimize relative drift before control activation. However, in the low-velocity regime, the allowable tolerances for release velocity and angular rate errors tighten significantly to satisfy distance constraints, making hardware requirements a critical bottleneck. To address this, we model the initialization sequence as a stochastic process and derive closed-form constraints on deployment errors and control activation intervals. These conditions ensure that inter-satellite distances remain within the allowable separation limit with a prescribed probability. Monte Carlo simulations, configured using the error bounds and intervals derived from the proposed constraints, demonstrate that inter-satellite distances are successfully maintained within the allowable range. The proposed framework enables the safe initialization of large-scale distributed space systems by translating strict separation constraints into quantifiable hardware requirements.

AI.tldr: A framework for designing formation initialization of large-scale distributed space systems that provides probabilistic safety guarantees by deriving closed-form constraints on deployment errors and control activation intervals to maintain inter-satellite distances within allowable separation limits.
AI.motivation: In large-scale distributed space systems using small satellites, achieving reliable transition to passively stable orbits while maintaining inter-satellite distances within effective control and communication ranges is crucial, especially given deployment errors and uncontrolled coasting phases. The challenge is that strict separation limits during initialization require low release velocities, which in turn tighten allowable tolerances for release velocity and angular rate errors, creating hardware requirement bottlenecks.
AI.method: The study models the initialization sequence as a stochastic process and derives closed-form constraints on deployment errors and control activation intervals. These conditions ensure inter-satellite distances remain within allowable separation limits with prescribed probability. Monte Carlo simulations are configured using error bounds and intervals derived from the proposed constraints.
AI.result: Monte Carlo simulations demonstrate that inter-satellite distances are successfully maintained within the allowable range. The framework enables safe initialization by translating strict separation constraints into quantifiable hardware requirements.
AI.conclusion: The proposed framework provides probabilistic safety guarantees for formation initialization of large-scale distributed space systems, addressing the critical bottleneck of hardware requirements in the low-velocity regime by deriving quantifiable constraints on deployment errors and control activation intervals.

title: A Manual Bar-by-Bar Tempo Measurement Protocol for Polyphonic Chamber Music Recordings: Design, Validation, and Application to Beethoven's Piano and Cello Sonatas
summary: Empirical performance analysis depends on the accurate extraction of tempo data from recordings, yet standard computational tools, designed for monophonic audio or modern studio conditions, fail systematically when applied to historical polyphonic chamber music. This paper documents the failure of automated beat-detection software on duo recordings of Beethoven's five piano and cello sonatas (Op.~5 Nos.~1 and~2; Op.~69; Op.~102 Nos.~1 and~2), and presents a formalised manual alternative: a cumulative lap-timer protocol that yields bar-level beats-per-minute data with millisecond resolution. The protocol, developed in cross-disciplinary collaboration with an engineer specialising in VLSI design, rests on a cumulative timestamp architecture that prevents error accumulation, permits internal self-validation, and captures expressive timing phenomena (rubato, fermatas, accelerandi, ritardandi) that automated tools systematically suppress or misread. The mathematical derivation of the BPM formula, the spreadsheet data structure, and the error characterisation are presented in full. Applied to over one hundred movement-level recordings spanning 1930--2012, the protocol generated a dataset subsequently visualised through tempographs, histograms with spline-smoothed probability density functions, ridgeline plots, and combination charts. The paper argues that manual annotation is not a methodological retreat but a principled response to the intrinsic limitations of computational tools when faced with the specific challenges of polyphonic historical recordings. The complete dataset and analysis code are publicly available.

AI.tldr: Manual beat-tracking protocol for historical polyphonic chamber music recordings where automated tools fail, using cumulative timestamp architecture to prevent error accumulation and capture expressive timing.
AI.motivation: Standard computational beat-detection tools fail systematically on historical polyphonic chamber music recordings, particularly for duo recordings of Beethoven's piano and cello sonatas, necessitating a reliable alternative for empirical tempo analysis.
AI.method: Developed a cumulative lap-timer protocol with millisecond resolution using cumulative timestamp architecture that prevents error accumulation, permits self-validation, and captures expressive timing phenomena (rubato, fermatas, accelerandi, ritardandi).
AI.result: Applied protocol to over 100 movement-level recordings (1930-2012), generating a dataset visualized through tempographs, histograms with spline-smoothed PDFs, ridgeline plots, and combination charts; complete dataset and analysis code made publicly available.
AI.conclusion: Manual annotation is a principled response to computational limitations for polyphonic historical recordings, not a methodological retreat; the protocol provides reliable bar-level BPM data with millisecond resolution where automated tools fail.

title: High Order Tuners for Adaptive Safety of Robotic Systems
summary: The combination of control barrier functions (CBFs) and adaptive control -- a framework referred to as adaptive safety -- has proven to be a powerful paradigm for safety-critical control of nonlinear systems with parametric uncertainties. Yet the theoretical conditions for forward invariance within this framework are often quite conservative, and may require using large adaptation gains to achieve acceptable performance, an approach that is traditionally discouraged in adaptive control. This paper mitigates these issues via high-order tuners, a recent class of higher-order adaptation laws that leverages different adaptation gains at different orders of differentiation. We illustrate that these high-order tuners decouple adaptation gain conditions from those placed on the initial conditions of the system required for set invariance. We extend these results to robotic systems whose linear-in-the-parameters structure proves particularly useful for adaptive control. The efficacy of our results are illustrated via simulations.

AI.tldr: High-order tuners reduce conservatism in adaptive safety control by decoupling adaptation gain conditions from initial condition requirements for set invariance.
AI.motivation: Traditional adaptive safety frameworks combining CBFs with adaptive control have conservative theoretical conditions for forward invariance, often requiring large adaptation gains that are discouraged in adaptive control practice.
AI.method: Use high-order tuners (higher-order adaptation laws) that leverage different adaptation gains at different orders of differentiation, extending the approach to robotic systems with linear-in-the-parameters structure.
AI.result: High-order tuners decouple adaptation gain conditions from initial condition requirements for set invariance, reducing conservatism and eliminating the need for excessively large adaptation gains.
AI.conclusion: High-order tuners provide an effective solution to mitigate conservatism in adaptive safety frameworks, enabling better performance without requiring large adaptation gains, particularly beneficial for robotic systems.

title: ClariCodec: Optimising Neural Speech Codes for 200bps Communication using Reinforcement Learning
summary: In bandwidth-constrained communication such as satellite and underwater channels, speech must often be transmitted at ultra-low bitrates where intelligibility is the primary objective. At such extreme compression levels, codecs trained with acoustic reconstruction losses tend to allocate bits to perceptual detail, leading to substantial degradation in word error rate (WER). This paper proposes ClariCodec, a neural speech codec operating at 200 bit per second (bps) that reformulates quantisation as a stochastic policy, enabling reinforcement learning (RL)-based optimisation of intelligibility. Specifically, the encoder is fine-tuned using WER-driven rewards while the acoustic reconstruction pipeline remains frozen. Even without RL, ClariCodec achieves 3.68% WER on the LibriSpeech test-clean set at 200 bps, already competitive with codecs operating at higher bitrates. Further RL fine-tuning reduces WER to 3.20% on test-clean and 8.93% on test-other, corresponding to a 13% relative reduction while preserving perceptual quality.

AI.tldr: ClariCodec is a 200 bps neural speech codec that uses reinforcement learning to optimize intelligibility by treating quantization as a stochastic policy, achieving state-of-the-art word error rates at ultra-low bitrates.
AI.motivation: In bandwidth-constrained environments like satellite and underwater channels, speech must be transmitted at ultra-low bitrates where intelligibility is paramount. Traditional codecs trained with acoustic reconstruction losses allocate bits to perceptual details at the expense of word error rate degradation.
AI.method: ClariCodec reformulates quantization as a stochastic policy, enabling reinforcement learning-based optimization of intelligibility. The encoder is fine-tuned using WER-driven rewards while keeping the acoustic reconstruction pipeline frozen. This allows direct optimization for intelligibility rather than acoustic fidelity.
AI.result: Without RL, ClariCodec achieves 3.68% WER on LibriSpeech test-clean at 200 bps, competitive with codecs at higher bitrates. RL fine-tuning further reduces WER to 3.20% on test-clean and 8.93% on test-other, a 13% relative reduction while preserving perceptual quality.
AI.conclusion: ClariCodec demonstrates that reformulating quantization as a stochastic policy enables effective RL-based optimization for intelligibility at ultra-low bitrates, achieving state-of-the-art performance while maintaining perceptual quality.

title: AC-OPF Feasibility Analysis and Sensitivity-Guided Capacitor Placement in a High-PV Islanded Microgrid
comment: 6 pages, 8 figures, 2 tables, under conference review
summary: This paper presents a comparative AC Optimal Power Flow study on a real world city scale islanded microgrid with high solar PV penetration, implemented within a Digital Twin framework. Four objective function cases economic dispatch, voltage stress exposure via PV power factor variation, then optimal load delivery, and capacitor enhanced economic dispatch as recovery options are evaluated over a 47 hour time series horizon on the same network under a shared loading scenario. Optimization sensitivities OSQ and OSV extracted from all cases are combined into a composite placement score used to rank candidate buses for shunt capacitor upgrades. A post processing planning optimization balances capacitor upgrade cost against avoided value-of-lost-load, enabling direct economic comparison of infrastructure investment versus reliability penalties. Results demonstrate that sensitivity guided capacitor placement restores full load service across the horizon and provides targeted reactive support at a quantifiable cost trade off against corrective load shedding.

AI.tldr: Comparative AC OPF study on islanded microgrid with high PV penetration using Digital Twin framework evaluates four objective functions for capacitor placement optimization to restore load service and provide reactive support.
AI.motivation: To address reliability challenges in real-world islanded microgrids with high solar PV penetration by developing a systematic approach for capacitor placement that balances infrastructure investment against reliability penalties.
AI.method: Digital Twin framework with comparative AC Optimal Power Flow study evaluating four objective functions (economic dispatch, voltage stress exposure via PV power factor variation, optimal load delivery, capacitor enhanced economic dispatch) over 47-hour time series. Optimization sensitivities (OSQ and OSV) combined into composite placement score to rank candidate buses for shunt capacitor upgrades, followed by planning optimization balancing upgrade cost against avoided value-of-lost-load.
AI.result: Sensitivity-guided capacitor placement restores full load service across the horizon and provides targeted reactive support with quantifiable cost trade-off against corrective load shedding.
AI.conclusion: The proposed methodology enables direct economic comparison of infrastructure investment versus reliability penalties, demonstrating effective capacitor placement for improved microgrid reliability in high PV penetration scenarios.

title: Listen, Pause, and Reason: Toward Perception-Grounded Hybrid Reasoning for Audio Understanding
summary: Recent Large Audio Language Models have demonstrated impressive capabilities in audio understanding. However, they often suffer from perceptual errors, while reliable audio reasoning is unattainable without first grounding the model's perception in structured auditory scenes. Inspired by Auditory Scene Analysis, we first introduce a Perception-Aware Question Answering (PAQA) dataset. PAQA implements a hierarchical decoupling strategy that separates speech from environmental sound and distinguishes multiple speakers, providing explicit perceptual reasoning for training. Building on this, we propose HyPeR, a two-stage Hybrid Perception-Reasoning framework. In Stage I, we finetune the model on PAQA to perceive acoustic attributes in complex audio. In Stage II, we leverage GRPO to refine the model's internal deliberation. We also introduce PAUSE tokens to facilitate latent computation during acoustically ambiguous phases and design perceptual consistency reward to align reasoning rationales with raw audio. Experiments across benchmarks demonstrate that HyPeR achieves absolute improvements over the base model, with performance comparable to large-scale models, stressing the effectiveness of hybrid perception-grounded reasoning for robust and multi-speaker audio understanding.

AI.tldr: HyPeR is a two-stage framework for audio language models that first improves perception via hierarchical decoupling of audio scenes, then refines reasoning with GRPO and perceptual consistency rewards.
AI.motivation: Current Large Audio Language Models suffer from perceptual errors and lack reliable audio reasoning because they don't ground perception in structured auditory scenes first.
AI.method: 1) Introduce PAQA dataset with hierarchical decoupling separating speech from environmental sound and distinguishing multiple speakers. 2) HyPeR framework: Stage I finetunes model on PAQA for acoustic attribute perception; Stage II uses GRPO to refine internal deliberation with PAUSE tokens for ambiguous phases and perceptual consistency rewards to align reasoning with raw audio.
AI.result: HyPeR achieves absolute improvements over base model across benchmarks, with performance comparable to large-scale models, demonstrating effectiveness of hybrid perception-grounded reasoning.
AI.conclusion: The hybrid perception-reasoning approach enables robust and multi-speaker audio understanding by first grounding perception in structured auditory scenes before reasoning.

title: Integrated Investment and Policy Planning for Power Systems via Differentiable Scenario Generation
summary: We formulate a method to co-optimize power system capacity planning decisions and policy investments that shape electricity load patterns. To this end, we leverage a gradient-based solution technique that enables the efficient solution of operation-aware planning models. To compute gradients with respect to the conditions that define daily electricity demand profiles, we introduce and formalize the concept of differentiable scenario generation and show that generative machine learning models satisfy the mathematical requirements needed to compute consistent gradients. We demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed approach through numerical experiments using a diffusion model-based scenario generator and a stylized generation and capacity expansion planning model.

AI.tldr: A method to co-optimize power system capacity planning and policy investments using differentiable scenario generation with generative ML models.
AI.motivation: To enable joint optimization of power system capacity planning decisions and policy investments that shape electricity load patterns, addressing the need for operation-aware planning models.
AI.method: Leverage gradient-based solution technique for efficient solution of operation-aware planning models; introduce differentiable scenario generation concept; use generative ML models (diffusion model-based scenario generator) to compute consistent gradients with respect to daily electricity demand profiles.
AI.result: Demonstrated feasibility through numerical experiments using diffusion model-based scenario generator and stylized generation and capacity expansion planning model.
AI.conclusion: The proposed approach enables co-optimization of power system planning and policy investments through differentiable scenario generation, providing a computationally efficient framework for operation-aware planning.

title: Quantifying and Improving the Accuracy of Electromagnetic Transient-Transient Stability Hybrid Simulation
comment: 12 pages, 25 figures, accepted by IEEE Transactions on Power Systems
summary: The increasing penetration of inverter-based resources introduces new dynamic challenges to modern power grids, such as sub- and super-synchronous oscillations and other faster dynamics. These dynamics are typically fast in nature and are difficult to accurately model and analyze using standard transient stability (TS) methods, necessitating the need for electromagnetic transient (EMT) analysis. However, EMT simulations are notoriously slow for large-scale grids due to both equation formulations and computational limitations. To overcome this challenge, EMT-TS hybrid simulation is often used, since it offers a balanced trade-off between accuracy and speed, making it feasible to perform EMT analysis on large systems. One open question about EMT-TS hybrid simulation is the accuracy of the EMT-TS boundary or interface. This paper introduces an error index to quantify EMT-TS hybrid interface errors, identifies conditions where the hybrid simulation approach may become inaccurate, and suggests EMT region expansions to improve the simulation accuracy. Additionally, a three-sequence hybrid interface model is proposed to mitigate inaccuracies caused by unbalanced conditions.

AI.tldr: This paper addresses accuracy issues in EMT-TS hybrid simulation for power grids with inverter-based resources, proposing an error index to quantify interface errors and suggesting EMT region expansions and a three-sequence interface model to improve accuracy.
AI.motivation: The increasing penetration of inverter-based resources introduces fast dynamics (sub-/super-synchronous oscillations) that are difficult to model with standard transient stability methods, requiring electromagnetic transient analysis. However, EMT simulations are slow for large grids, leading to the use of EMT-TS hybrid simulation, but the accuracy of the EMT-TS boundary/interface remains an open question.
AI.method: The paper introduces an error index to quantify EMT-TS hybrid interface errors, identifies conditions where hybrid simulation becomes inaccurate, suggests EMT region expansions to improve accuracy, and proposes a three-sequence hybrid interface model to mitigate inaccuracies caused by unbalanced conditions.
AI.result: The proposed error index quantifies interface errors, conditions for inaccuracy are identified, EMT region expansions are suggested to improve simulation accuracy, and a three-sequence interface model is developed to address unbalanced condition issues.
AI.conclusion: The paper provides tools to assess and improve EMT-TS hybrid simulation accuracy through error quantification, condition identification, region expansion recommendations, and a three-sequence interface model, addressing critical accuracy concerns in modeling modern power grids with inverter-based resources.

title: Energy-based Regularization for Learning Residual Dynamics in Neural MPC for Omnidirectional Aerial Robots
summary: Data-driven Model Predictive Control (MPC) has lately been the core research subject in the field of control theory. The combination of an optimal control framework with deep learning paradigms opens up the possibility to accurately track control tasks without the need for complex analytical models. However, the system dynamics are often nuanced and the neural model lacks the potential to understand physical properties such as inertia and conservation of energy. In this work, we propose a novel energy-based regularization loss function which is applied to the training of a neural model that learns the residual dynamics of an omnidirectional aerial robot. Our energy-based regularization encourages the neural network to cause control corrections that stabilize the energy of the system. The residual dynamics are integrated into the MPC framework and improve the positional mean absolute error (MAE) over three real-world experiments by 23% compared to an analytical MPC. We also compare our method to a standard neural MPC implementation without regularization and primarily achieve a significantly increased flight stability implicitly due to the energy regularization and up to 15% lower MAE. Our code is available under: https://github.com/johanneskbl/jsk_aerial_robot/tree/develop/neural_MPC.

AI.tldr: Energy-based regularization for neural MPC improves aerial robot control by stabilizing system energy, achieving 23% lower MAE than analytical MPC and 15% better than unregularized neural MPC.
AI.motivation: Data-driven MPC with neural networks can track control tasks without complex analytical models, but neural models often fail to capture physical properties like inertia and energy conservation, leading to suboptimal performance.
AI.method: Proposes an energy-based regularization loss function applied to training a neural model that learns residual dynamics of an omnidirectional aerial robot. The regularization encourages control corrections that stabilize system energy, with residual dynamics integrated into MPC framework.
AI.result: Improves positional mean absolute error (MAE) by 23% compared to analytical MPC across three real-world experiments. Compared to standard neural MPC without regularization, achieves up to 15% lower MAE and significantly increased flight stability.
AI.conclusion: Energy-based regularization effectively incorporates physical principles into neural MPC, enhancing both accuracy and stability for aerial robot control, demonstrating the value of physics-informed regularization in data-driven control systems.

title: Temporal Logic Resilience for Continuous-time Systems
summary: In this paper, we present a novel framework for quantifying a lower bound on resilience in continuous-time (non)linear systems subject to external disturbances while ensuring satisfaction of signal temporal logic specifications. Unlike robustness, which evaluates how well a system satisfies a specification under a given disturbance, resilience measures the maximum disturbance a system can tolerate from a given initial state while maintaining specification satisfaction. We first derive bounds on the perturbed trajectories and then use them to formulate a computational method based on scenario optimization to efficiently compute the maximum admissible disturbance. We validate our approach through case studies, including dc motor, temperature regulation, a nonlinear numerical example, and a vehicle collision avoidance case.

AI.tldr: A framework for quantifying lower bounds on resilience in continuous-time (non)linear systems under disturbances while ensuring satisfaction of signal temporal logic specifications.
AI.motivation: Existing robustness metrics evaluate specification satisfaction under given disturbances, but resilience measures the maximum disturbance a system can tolerate from an initial state while maintaining specification satisfaction. There's a need to quantify this resilience property for safety-critical systems.
AI.method: First derive bounds on perturbed trajectories, then use these bounds to formulate a computational method based on scenario optimization to efficiently compute the maximum admissible disturbance.
AI.result: The approach is validated through case studies including DC motor, temperature regulation, a nonlinear numerical example, and a vehicle collision avoidance scenario.
AI.conclusion: The proposed framework successfully quantifies lower bounds on resilience for continuous-time (non)linear systems subject to disturbances while ensuring satisfaction of signal temporal logic specifications.

title: Co-Design of Cryptographic Parameters and Delay-Aware Feedback Gain for Encrypted Control Systems
comment: 6 pages, 3 figures, 2 tables, submitted to SICE FES 2026
summary: Encrypted control employs homomorphic encryption (HE) to protect both the computation and communication stages, making it a promising approach for secure networked control systems. Most existing results pre-design a controller in the plaintext domain and then implement it over encrypted data. However, this can be problematic because HE induces non-negligible communication and computation delays, which typically increase with the security level, potentially degrading control performance and even destabilizing the closed-loop system. To address this issue, we propose a co-design framework for cryptographic parameters and delay-aware feedback gain. We characterize the encryption-induced delay as a function of the cryptographic parameters and derive a sufficient condition for the existence of a stabilizing delay-aware feedback gain, expressed as a finite set of linear matrix inequalities. This leads to a tractable outer-inner design procedure that searches over cryptographic parameters that satisfy a desired security level and, for each such parameter, seeks a stabilizing feedback gain.

AI.tldr: Co-design framework for cryptographic parameters and delay-aware feedback gain in encrypted control systems to address HE-induced delays.
AI.motivation: Homomorphic encryption in control systems introduces communication and computation delays that increase with security level, potentially degrading performance and destabilizing closed-loop systems. Existing approaches that pre-design controllers in plaintext domain then implement over encrypted data are problematic due to these delays.
AI.method: Characterize encryption-induced delay as function of cryptographic parameters, derive sufficient condition for existence of stabilizing delay-aware feedback gain expressed as linear matrix inequalities, develop tractable outer-inner design procedure that searches over cryptographic parameters satisfying desired security level and seeks stabilizing feedback gain for each parameter.
AI.result: Proposed co-design framework addresses HE-induced delay problem by jointly optimizing cryptographic parameters and feedback gain, with sufficient stability condition expressed as LMIs enabling systematic design procedure.
AI.conclusion: The co-design approach enables secure networked control systems with homomorphic encryption while maintaining stability and performance by accounting for encryption-induced delays in controller design.

title: Towards Trustworthy 6G Network Digital Twins: A Framework for Validating Counterfactual What-If Analysis in Edge Computing Resources
summary: Network Digital Twins (NDTs) enable safe what-if analysis for 6G cloud-edge infrastructures, but adoption is often limited by fragmented workflows from telemetry to validation. We present a data-driven NDT framework that extends 6G-TWIN with a scalable pipeline for cloud-edge telemetry aggregation and semantic alignment into unified data models. Our contributions include: (i) scalable cloud-edge telemetry collection, (ii) regime-aware feature engineering capturing the network's scaling behavior, and (iii) a validation methodology based on Sign Agreement and Directional Sensitivity. Evaluated on a Kubernetes-managed cluster, the framework extrapolates performance to unseen high-load regimes. Results show both Deep Neural Network (DNN) and XGBoost achieve high regression accuracy (R2 > 0.99), while the XGBoost model delivers superior directional reliability (Sa > 0.90), making the NDT a trustworthy tool for proactive resource scaling in out-of-distribution scenarios.

AI.tldr: A data-driven Network Digital Twin framework for 6G cloud-edge infrastructures that enables trustworthy what-if analysis through scalable telemetry aggregation, regime-aware feature engineering, and validation metrics for out-of-distribution scenarios.
AI.motivation: Network Digital Twins (NDTs) enable safe what-if analysis for 6G cloud-edge infrastructures, but adoption is limited by fragmented workflows from telemetry to validation. There's a need for unified data models and validation methodologies to make NDTs trustworthy for proactive resource scaling.
AI.method: Extends 6G-TWIN with a scalable pipeline for cloud-edge telemetry aggregation and semantic alignment into unified data models. Includes: (i) scalable cloud-edge telemetry collection, (ii) regime-aware feature engineering capturing network scaling behavior, and (iii) validation methodology based on Sign Agreement and Directional Sensitivity metrics.
AI.result: Evaluated on a Kubernetes-managed cluster, the framework extrapolates performance to unseen high-load regimes. Both DNN and XGBoost achieve high regression accuracy (R2 > 0.99), while XGBoost delivers superior directional reliability (Sa > 0.90), making the NDT trustworthy for proactive resource scaling in out-of-distribution scenarios.
AI.conclusion: The proposed data-driven NDT framework successfully addresses workflow fragmentation in 6G cloud-edge infrastructures by providing scalable telemetry aggregation, semantic alignment, and robust validation metrics. XGBoost models demonstrate superior directional reliability for trustworthy what-if analysis and proactive resource management in unseen operational regimes.

title: CBF-based Probabilistic Safe Navigation under Unknown Nonlinear Obstacle Dynamics
comment: 6 pages, 2 figures. Submitted to IEEE L-CSS with CDC 2026 option
summary: Safe navigation for an ego vehicle in uncertain environments characterized by dynamic obstacles with unknown nonlinear dynamics is a challenging problem of significant practical interest. Existing approaches in the literature either lack formal safety guarantees, require full model knowledge, or fail to account for the risk associated with the vehicle's exact body geometry and the temporal evolution of uncertainty between sampling instants. In this paper, we propose a data-driven observer for the unknown obstacle dynamics that generates an alpha-confidence set flow, which is exactly transformed into a Control Barrier Function (CBF) to enforce (1-alpha)-probability safety. The proposed framework accommodates nonlinear ego vehicle dynamics of arbitrary relative degree, as demonstrated through case studies involving first- and second-order dynamics of an unmanned surface vehicle.

AI.tldr: A data-driven observer with alpha-confidence sets and Control Barrier Functions ensures (1-alpha)-probability safety for ego vehicles navigating dynamic obstacles with unknown nonlinear dynamics.
AI.motivation: Safe navigation in uncertain environments with dynamic obstacles having unknown nonlinear dynamics lacks formal safety guarantees, full model knowledge requirements, or proper risk accounting for vehicle geometry and temporal uncertainty evolution.
AI.method: Data-driven observer for unknown obstacle dynamics generates alpha-confidence set flow, transformed into Control Barrier Functions to enforce (1-alpha)-probability safety; accommodates nonlinear ego vehicle dynamics of arbitrary relative degree.
AI.result: Demonstrated through case studies involving first- and second-order dynamics of an unmanned surface vehicle, showing the framework's applicability to real-world navigation scenarios.
AI.conclusion: The proposed framework provides formal probabilistic safety guarantees for ego vehicles navigating uncertain environments with unknown dynamic obstacles, addressing limitations of existing approaches.

title: Generalizability of Learning-based Occupancy Detection in Residential Buildings
comment: 8 pages, 8 Figures, 4 Tables, Accepted for publication in the proceedings of the 2026 IFAC World Congress, Busan, Republic of Korea
summary: This paper investigates non-intrusive occupancy detection methods for residential buildings using environmental sensor data from the KTH Live-In Lab in Stockholm, Sweden. Three machine learning approaches, namely, logistic regression (LR), support vector machines (SVM), and long short-term memory (LSTM) network enhanced with an attention mechanism, are evaluated in terms of predictive performance and computational complexity. The analysis considers the trade-off between sensor availability (investment cost) and prediction accuracy in real applications, as well as the models' cross-apartment generalizability. Hyperparameters for both the SVM and LSTM models are optimized using Bayesian optimization. All three models are evaluated on data collected from apartments not used during training, and on data generated from a calibrated digital model of the testbed. Results show that all models achieve comparable performance on the same-apartment test data (accuracy of approximately 0.83, F1 score of approximately 0.86). When assessed on cross-apartment data, the LSTM model demonstrates the strongest generalization capability (accuracy of 0.84, F1 score of 0.85), while LR provides a competitive, low-complexity alternative for applications that do not require cross-apartment generalization.

AI.tldr: Non-intrusive occupancy detection using environmental sensor data from KTH Live-In Lab, comparing LR, SVM, and attention-enhanced LSTM models for performance, computational complexity, and cross-apartment generalization.
AI.motivation: To develop non-intrusive occupancy detection methods for residential buildings that balance sensor availability (cost) with prediction accuracy, while evaluating models' cross-apartment generalizability for practical applications.
AI.method: Three ML approaches: logistic regression, SVM, and LSTM with attention mechanism. Hyperparameters optimized via Bayesian optimization. Models evaluated on unseen apartment data and calibrated digital model data from KTH Live-In Lab.
AI.result: All models achieved comparable performance on same-apartment test data (~0.83 accuracy, ~0.86 F1). LSTM showed strongest cross-apartment generalization (0.84 accuracy, 0.85 F1), while LR provided competitive low-complexity alternative for non-generalization applications.
AI.conclusion: LSTM with attention mechanism offers best cross-apartment generalization for occupancy detection, but LR provides a computationally efficient alternative when cross-apartment generalization is not required, enabling cost-effective sensor deployment decisions.

title: Simplification Ad Absurdum? Revisiting Gas Flow Modeling for Integrated Energy System Planning
summary: This paper analyzes the implications of simplified pipeline gas flow models for integrated energy system planning. A case study of an integrated power-hydrogen expansion planning problem shows that simplifying pressure-flow relationships and gas dynamics can lead to expansion plans that incur substantial regret when evaluated under a more realistic dynamic gas flow model -- due to suboptimal system expansion, operation, and non-supplied hydrogen. Numerical experiments show that planning under the highly simplified transport and transport-linepack models -- commonly used in expansion studies -- can result in regret exceeding several thousand percent and yield expansion plans that lack robustness across demand levels. Planning under steady-state conditions partially mitigates these effects, but still leaves significant cost-reduction potential untapped compared to dynamic planning due to neglected linepack flexibility. Developing efficient solution algorithms for the dynamic model is a promising direction for future research.

AI.tldr: Simplified gas flow models in integrated energy system planning lead to suboptimal expansion plans with high regret when evaluated under realistic dynamic models.
AI.motivation: To analyze the implications of simplified pipeline gas flow models for integrated energy system planning, particularly how simplifications affect expansion plan quality and robustness.
AI.method: Case study approach using an integrated power-hydrogen expansion planning problem, comparing different gas flow model simplifications (transport, transport-linepack, steady-state) against a realistic dynamic gas flow model.
AI.result: Highly simplified models (transport and transport-linepack) cause regret exceeding several thousand percent and yield non-robust expansion plans. Steady-state planning partially mitigates effects but still leaves significant cost-reduction potential untapped compared to dynamic planning.
AI.conclusion: Simplified gas flow models lead to substantial suboptimality in expansion planning; dynamic planning that accounts for linepack flexibility is superior; developing efficient solution algorithms for dynamic models is a promising research direction.

title: Data-driven Linear Quadratic Integral Control: A Convex Formulation and Policy Gradient Approach
summary: This paper studies the data-driven synthesis of linear quadratic integral (LQI) controllers for continuous-time systems. The objective is to achieve optimal state-feedback control with integral action for reference tracking using only measured data. To this end, we derive a data-driven closed-loop parameterization of the augmented dynamics that incorporates the integral state while relying solely on input-state-output measurements of the underlying system. Based on this parameterization, a data-driven convex optimization problem is formulated whose solution yields the optimal linear quadratic regulator (LQR) feedback gain for the augmented system without explicit knowledge of the system matrices. In addition, a policy gradient flow is derived to compute the optimal controller within the space of stabilizing gains. The proposed approach enables data-driven optimal tracking control while avoiding explicit state augmentation in the data collection phase. The effectiveness of the method is demonstrated through a numerical example involving a distributed generation unit (DGU) in a DC microgrid.

AI.tldr: Data-driven synthesis of LQI controllers for continuous-time systems using only measured data, without requiring system matrices or explicit state augmentation during data collection.
AI.motivation: To achieve optimal state-feedback control with integral action for reference tracking using only measured data, avoiding the need for explicit system identification or state augmentation during data collection.
AI.method: Derived a data-driven closed-loop parameterization of augmented dynamics incorporating integral state using input-state-output measurements. Formulated a convex optimization problem to compute optimal LQR feedback gain for augmented system without system matrices. Also derived a policy gradient flow to compute optimal controller within stabilizing gain space.
AI.result: The approach enables data-driven optimal tracking control without explicit state augmentation in data collection phase. Effectiveness demonstrated through numerical example involving a distributed generation unit in a DC microgrid.
AI.conclusion: Proposed method successfully achieves data-driven synthesis of LQI controllers for continuous-time systems, providing optimal tracking control using only measured data while avoiding explicit system identification and state augmentation requirements.

authors: Paul M. J. Van den Hof
title: Modelling and identification of diffusively coupled linear networks with additional directed links
summary: Dynamic networks consist of interconnected dynamical systems. The subsystems can be viewed as transformations of input signals into output signals, where signals flow from one system into another through interconnections. The signal flows represent directions of information flow, thus a dynamic network can be visualised by a directed graph. In contrast, natural and physical laws only impose relations between systems variables, while variables are shared among systems via interconnections. Sharing is independent of direction, and therefore a dynamic network originating from physics can be visualised by an undirected graph. Typically, dynamic networks are considered to have either directed or undirected interconnections. For both situations, network models, analytic tools, and identification algorithms have been developed. However, dynamic networks can also have both directed and undirected interconnections, for example, in physical networks equipped with digital controllers. In this work, we present mixed linear dynamic networks that contain both undirected and directed interconnections, where the nature of the interconnecting dynamics needs to be incorporated into the modelling framework, identifiability analysis, and identification procedure. For these mixed networks, we derive dynamic network models; formulate conditions for consistent identification of all dynamics in the network; and develop a tractable identification algorithm that delivers consistent estimates.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces mixed linear dynamic networks containing both directed and undirected interconnections, develops models for them, establishes identifiability conditions, and creates a consistent identification algorithm.
AI.motivation: Traditional dynamic network modeling treats interconnections as either directed (information flow) or undirected (physical variable sharing), but real-world networks like physical systems with digital controllers contain both types, requiring new modeling and identification frameworks.
AI.method: Develops dynamic network models for mixed networks with both directed and undirected interconnections, incorporates the nature of interconnecting dynamics into the modeling framework, formulates identifiability conditions, and creates a tractable identification algorithm.
AI.result: Derives dynamic network models for mixed networks, establishes conditions for consistent identification of all dynamics, and develops an identification algorithm that delivers consistent estimates.
AI.conclusion: The paper provides a comprehensive framework for modeling, analyzing, and identifying mixed linear dynamic networks with both directed and undirected interconnections, addressing a gap in existing network theory for hybrid physical-digital systems.

title: Minimal Input Cardinality Disturbance Decoupling of Coupled Oscillators via Output Feedback with Application to Power Networks
comment: Manuscript accepted for publication in the proceedings of the 23rd IFAC World Congress, Busan, Republic of Korea, 2026
summary: In this paper, we identify the smallest set of control input nodes and an associated output feedback law that achieves complete disturbance decoupling for a class of coupled oscillator networks. The focus is specifically on systems linearized around a stable phase-locked synchronized state. The proposed theoretical framework is applied to the linearized swing dynamics of power grids operating near synchronization. In this context, the disturbance decoupling problem corresponds to isolating subsets of nodes from exogenous disturbances by means of batteries that can both add or withdraw active power. Numerical simulations carried out on the IEEE New England 39-bus system show that the proposed methodology not only yields a minimal actuator placement ensuring effective disturbance rejection, but also preserves the internal stability of the closed-loop system.

AI.tldr: Minimal actuator placement and output feedback for disturbance decoupling in coupled oscillator networks, applied to power grid swing dynamics with battery control.
AI.motivation: Address the need for efficient disturbance isolation in coupled oscillator networks, particularly in power grids where disturbances can propagate and cause instability. Focus on finding minimal control resources to achieve complete disturbance decoupling while maintaining system stability.
AI.method: Develop theoretical framework for identifying smallest set of control input nodes and associated output feedback law achieving complete disturbance decoupling for coupled oscillator networks linearized around stable phase-locked synchronized states. Applied to linearized swing dynamics of power grids with battery-based active power control.
AI.result: Methodology yields minimal actuator placement ensuring effective disturbance rejection while preserving internal stability of closed-loop system. Numerical simulations on IEEE New England 39-bus system demonstrate practical effectiveness.
AI.conclusion: Proposed framework successfully identifies minimal control resources for disturbance decoupling in coupled oscillator networks, with practical application to power grid stability through battery-based control that isolates subsets of nodes from exogenous disturbances.

title: Degradation-aware Predictive Energy Management for Fuel Cell-Battery Ship Power System with Data-driven Load Forecasting
summary: Hydrogen-based zero-emission ships are a key element in the decarbonization of the maritime sector. To strengthen these their economic competitiveness, it is key to drive their costs to a minimum. Current literature mainly focuses on fuel consumption minimization, but there is a lack of explicit consideration of costs arising from cell degradation and optimization-based approaches that leverage information on future load trajectories. This work aims at minimizing the operational cost of fuel cell-battery hybrid shipboard power systems, accounting for hydrogen consumption and cell degradation as the main cost drivers. A degradation-aware predictive energy management strategy utilizing data-driven load forecasting is designed and showcased at the example of a virtually retrofitted harbor tug. This work shows that the real onboard measurements of the vessel can be utilized to make accurate load predictions over 15min. Results indicate that the degradation-aware, predictive control simultaneously reduces the hydrogen consumption by up to 5.8% and the cell degradation by up to 36.4% with an aged fuel cell system when compared to a filter-based benchmark applied to real operating data of the harbor tug. With an increased prediction horizon of 1h, further significant reductions of 3.8% and 14.0% could be shown.

AI.tldr: A predictive energy management strategy for hydrogen fuel cell-battery hybrid ships that minimizes operational costs by optimizing hydrogen consumption and fuel cell degradation using load forecasting.
AI.motivation: Current literature focuses mainly on fuel consumption minimization but lacks explicit consideration of fuel cell degradation costs and optimization approaches that leverage future load trajectory information, which is crucial for improving the economic competitiveness of hydrogen-based zero-emission ships.
AI.method: A degradation-aware predictive energy management strategy utilizing data-driven load forecasting was designed and applied to a virtually retrofitted harbor tug. The approach uses real onboard measurements to make accurate load predictions and optimizes operational costs considering both hydrogen consumption and cell degradation.
AI.result: The method achieved accurate load predictions over 15 minutes using real onboard measurements. Compared to a filter-based benchmark, the degradation-aware predictive control reduced hydrogen consumption by up to 5.8% and cell degradation by up to 36.4% with an aged fuel cell system. With a 1-hour prediction horizon, further reductions of 3.8% and 14.0% were achieved.
AI.conclusion: The proposed degradation-aware predictive energy management strategy effectively reduces both hydrogen consumption and fuel cell degradation costs, demonstrating significant improvements over conventional approaches and highlighting the value of leveraging load forecasting for optimizing hybrid shipboard power systems.

title: On-Line Policy Iteration with Trajectory-Driven Policy Generation
summary: We consider deterministic finite-horizon optimal control problems with a fixed initial state. We introduce an on-line policy iteration method, which starting from a given policy, however obtained, generates a sequence of cost improving policies and corresponding trajectories. Each policy produces a trajectory, which is used in turn to generate data for training the next policy. The method is motivated by problems that are repeatedly solved starting from the same initial state, including discrete optimization and path planning for repetitive tasks. For such problems, the method is fast enough to be used on-line. Under a natural consistency condition, we show that the sequence of costs of the generated policies is monotonically improving for the given initial state (but not necessarily for other states). We illustrate our results with computational studies from combinatorial optimization and 3-dimensional path planning for drones in the presence of obstacles. We also discuss briefly a stochastic counterpart of our algorithm. Our proposed framework combines elements of rollout and policy iteration with flexible trajectory-based policy representations, and applies to problems involving a single as well as multiple decision makers. It also provides a principled way to train neural network-based policies using trajectory data, while preserving monotonic cost improvement.

AI.tldr: An on-line policy iteration method for deterministic finite-horizon optimal control with fixed initial state, generating cost-improving policies using trajectory data for repetitive tasks.
AI.motivation: Address problems repeatedly solved from the same initial state (discrete optimization, path planning for repetitive tasks) where fast on-line solutions are needed.
