AI.method: On-line policy iteration starting from any policy, using each policy's trajectory to generate training data for the next policy, combining rollout and policy iteration with flexible trajectory-based policy representations.
AI.result: Under consistency condition, sequence of policy costs is monotonically improving for the given initial state; validated with computational studies in combinatorial optimization and 3D drone path planning with obstacles.
AI.conclusion: Framework enables fast on-line policy improvement for repetitive tasks, supports neural network policy training with monotonic cost improvement, and extends to multi-agent problems and stochastic variants.

title: Nonlinear backstepping with saturation for low-thrust station-keeping of libration point orbits
comment: Preprint submitted to Acta Astronautica. For a working demo of the solution proposed, see https://github.com/antoniownunes/NL_SK_mwe
summary: This paper presents a novel nonlinear backstepping control law for continuous, low-thrust station-keeping in the Earth-Moon system. Quasi-periodic libration point orbits are targeted under a high-fidelity model of the dynamics. Almost global uniform exponential stability guarantees are attained, as shown through Lyapunov's stability theory. Saturation of the actuators is formally included in the controller design, such that these guarantees hold even in the event of saturation. The relationship between saturation threshold, control gains, and deviation is studied and an optimal procedure for gain selection is discussed. The control solution is tested numerically through a Monte Carlo analysis over representative application cases, subject to operational errors, constraints, and external perturbations. Station-keeping under actuation saturation is validated considering a conservative threshold for typical electric propulsion systems.

AI.tldr: Novel nonlinear backstepping control for continuous low-thrust station-keeping in Earth-Moon system targeting quasi-periodic libration point orbits with almost global uniform exponential stability guarantees under actuator saturation.
AI.motivation: To develop a robust station-keeping control solution for continuous low-thrust spacecraft in the Earth-Moon system that can handle quasi-periodic libration point orbits under high-fidelity dynamics while accounting for actuator saturation constraints typical of electric propulsion systems.
AI.method: Nonlinear backstepping control law design with formal inclusion of actuator saturation in controller formulation. Lyapunov stability theory is used to prove almost global uniform exponential stability. The relationship between saturation threshold, control gains, and deviation is analyzed, and an optimal gain selection procedure is developed. Numerical validation through Monte Carlo analysis over representative application cases with operational errors, constraints, and external perturbations.
AI.result: The controller achieves almost global uniform exponential stability guarantees even under actuator saturation. Station-keeping performance is validated numerically with conservative saturation thresholds for typical electric propulsion systems. The optimal gain selection procedure enables effective control performance while respecting saturation constraints.
AI.conclusion: The proposed nonlinear backstepping control provides a robust solution for continuous low-thrust station-keeping in the Earth-Moon system, with formal stability guarantees that hold even under actuator saturation, making it suitable for practical applications with electric propulsion systems.

title: A Nonlinear Separation Principle: Applications to Neural Networks, Control and Learning
comment: arXiv admin note: text overlap with arXiv:2604.00119
summary: This paper investigates continuous-time and discrete-time firing-rate and Hopfield recurrent neural networks (RNNs), with applications in nonlinear control design and implicit deep learning. First, we introduce a nonlinear separation principle that guarantees global exponential stability for the interconnection of a contracting state-feedback controller and a contracting observer, alongside parametric extensions for robustness and equilibrium tracking. Second, we derive sharp linear matrix inequality (LMI) conditions that guarantee the contractivity of both firing rate and Hopfield neural network architectures. We establish structural relationships among these certificates-demonstrating that continuous-time models with monotone non-decreasing activations maximize the admissible weight space, and extend these stability guarantees to interconnected systems and Graph RNNs. Third, we combine our separation principle and LMI framework to solve the output reference tracking problem for RNN-modeled plants. We provide LMI synthesis methods for feedback controllers and observers, and rigorously design a low-gain integral controller to eliminate steady-state error. Finally, we derive an exact, unconstrained algebraic parameterization of our contraction LMIs to design highly expressive implicit neural networks, achieving competitive accuracy and parameter efficiency on standard image classification benchmarks.

AI.tldr: The paper develops a contraction theory framework for firing-rate and Hopfield RNNs, introducing a nonlinear separation principle and LMI-based contractivity conditions, with applications to control design and implicit deep learning.
AI.motivation: To establish rigorous stability guarantees for recurrent neural networks (both firing-rate and Hopfield architectures) that enable their reliable application in nonlinear control systems and implicit deep learning models, addressing the need for provable stability in RNN-based systems.
AI.method: Develops a contraction theory framework with: 1) A nonlinear separation principle for interconnected contracting systems, 2) Sharp LMI conditions for contractivity of RNN architectures, 3) Structural analysis of weight space relationships, 4) Extension to Graph RNNs and interconnected systems, 5) LMI synthesis methods for controllers and observers, 6) Low-gain integral controller design for steady-state error elimination, 7) Unconstrained algebraic parameterization of contraction LMIs for implicit neural networks.
AI.result: Establishes global exponential stability guarantees for interconnected contracting systems, demonstrates that continuous-time models with monotone non-decreasing activations maximize admissible weight space, provides exact LMI conditions for RNN contractivity, solves output reference tracking problems for RNN-modeled plants, and achieves competitive accuracy and parameter efficiency on image classification benchmarks with implicit neural networks.
AI.conclusion: The paper provides a comprehensive contraction-based framework for analyzing and designing stable RNN systems, unifying control theory and deep learning perspectives, with demonstrated effectiveness in both control applications and implicit neural network design for classification tasks.

title: Tube-Based Robust Data-Driven Predictive Control
summary: This paper presents a tractable tube-based robust data-driven predictive control scheme that uses only a single finite noisy input-state trajectory of an unknown discrete-time linear time-invariant (LTI) system. A simplex constraint is imposed on the Hankel coefficient vector, yielding explicit polyhedral bounds on the prediction mismatch induced by bounded measurement noise. Using certified initial and terminal robust positively invariant (RPI) sets, we derive a tube-tightened formulation whose online optimization problem is a strictly convex quadratic program (QP). The resulting controller guarantees recursive feasibility, robust satisfaction of input and state constraints, and practical input-to-state stability of the closed loop with respect to measurement noise. Numerical examples illustrate the effectiveness, robustness, and closed-loop performance of the proposed method.

AI.tldr: Tube-based robust data-driven predictive control using single noisy trajectory with simplex constraint on Hankel coefficients, ensuring recursive feasibility and practical input-to-state stability.
AI.motivation: To develop a robust data-driven predictive control scheme that works with only a single finite noisy input-state trajectory of an unknown LTI system, addressing the challenge of handling measurement noise while maintaining constraint satisfaction and stability guarantees.
AI.method: Uses tube-based robust data-driven predictive control with simplex constraint on Hankel coefficient vector to obtain explicit polyhedral bounds on prediction mismatch. Incorporates certified initial and terminal robust positively invariant (RPI) sets to create a tube-tightened formulation solved as a strictly convex quadratic program (QP).
AI.result: The controller guarantees recursive feasibility, robust satisfaction of input and state constraints, and practical input-to-state stability with respect to measurement noise. Numerical examples demonstrate effectiveness, robustness, and closed-loop performance.
AI.conclusion: The proposed method provides a tractable robust data-driven predictive control scheme that requires only minimal data (single noisy trajectory) while delivering strong theoretical guarantees and practical performance.
